toolProblems: javascript_tool silently corrupts long string literals that contain repeated character runs: a 19,644-char base64 JPEG arrived 1,071 chars short (decoded 15,536 bytes instead of 14,732) and a second attempt lost 284 bytes. The first corruption was only discovered AFTER upload, creating one unintended Asset (01M2N4SPM1NKG2GGZTTCGNWXR4). Mitigation used for everything after: gzip the file (high-entropy, no runs), base64 that, split into ≤5,568-char chunks whose length is verified in-page, decompress via DecompressionStream, and hash-guard before dispatching — abort on mismatch. All later uploads matched byte-exactly.

The Browser pane was hidden for part of the run, so coordinate clicks failed with 'not compositing frames' and tabs_select did not help. Non-spending product controls ('Use whole video', 'Cancel') were therefore activated via their own button elements. No spending control was ever activated this way.

Page CSP blocks connect-src to anything but the app origin: fetching a localhost helper server failed, and fetching the product's own media URL fails because it redirects cross-origin to object storage (opaqueredirect). This is what prevented the byte-for-byte download comparison in REAL-12.

The in-app Browser has no file_upload tool, so uploads had to be injected into the product's own hidden file input via DataTransfer. The upload still goes through the product's real client action (uploadFilesDirect -> authorizeUpload -> finalize); only the OS file picker is bypassed.
findings: Staging redeployed TWICE during this group (eed4f079 -> 4496bc3b at ~13:13Z -> 57ce7ee6 at ~13:24Z, both real main merges: PR #1460 and PR #1455), including a window where the app served a blank page. The build the round is supposed to test no longer exists on staging. Nothing after ~13:13Z can be attributed to eed4f079, and any later R3 group will silently test a different build unless staging is pinned or the round is re-baselined. This is the single most important result of this group.

Deploy-time upload failure with a misleading message (product defect, merchant-visible): after a redeploy, an already-open page's server actions return 404 and EVERY upload from that page fails with 'Reference couldn't be attached — We couldn't upload that file. Check your connection and try again.' I confirmed the cause by instrumenting fetch (two POSTs to the page route, both 404, no storage request attempted) and confirmed the cure is a reload: identical bytes that failed repeatedly uploaded first try on a freshly loaded page. The copy blames the merchant's connection for a deploy-side condition, and it cost me ~25 minutes of misdiagnosis (I first believed video upload was broken). Suggest detecting the stale-action 404 and prompting a reload instead.

Dead-end product creation path (merchant-visible): the product surface tells merchants to create products in Brand — OttoStuff's 'Set as product image' empty state renders 'No products yet — add one in Brand memory' linking to BRAND_MEMORY_HREF, and lib/exits.ts still documents it as "'Your products' 下的 '+ Add product' 在这个视图里" (apps/web/components/otto/OttoStuff.tsx:468–472, apps/web/lib/exits.ts:38–39). The shipped /brand shell has only Brand voice / Audiences / Knowledge base / Style guide / Visual guidelines — no products section — and Library > Elements > Products is read-only ('Elements you and Otto save while creating show up here'). So a merchant who follows the product's own instruction lands somewhere with no such control, and there is no human way to create a product. The backing action (saveBrandRecord kind='product' -> createProduct, apps/web/lib/brand-record-actions.ts:228–240) is intact, so this is a missing/unwired UI, not a missing capability. This blocks REAL-03.

Uploading a video silently writes a brand-memory fact (merchant-visible, privacy/quality): the auto-understanding of my throwaway 3-second orange test clip wrote Memory row 01M2N6Y9NEK11F406B9WDJFF2S (category 'about', source 'otto') containing 'The video displays a solid orange screen with no other visual elements.', and it now renders on /brand as a Brand voice context marked 'Ready / Saved by Otto'. The three image uploads produced no such row. So one reference-clip upload injects an unreviewed sentence into the brand knowledge Otto writes from, with no confirmation step at upload time. Worth a Founder ruling on whether video understanding should propose (draft) rather than save.

No price disclosure at the upload entry itself: uploading charges 0.1 credits per file immediately (reserve+settle within ~3 s of the scan), but neither /create's 'Add a reference' nor the canvas 'Attach a file' shows any price near the control — the disclosure now lives only on /billing (consistent with the R3-F06 change, commit eed4f079, which removed the persistent cost notes near the input). FRONT-A1 still lists '上传入口价目小字' as a money-engine delivery surface, so if that acceptance row is still live, it and R3-F06 now disagree. Flagging for the Founder rather than assuming which one wins.

Byte validation only sniffs the header (low severity, self-inflicted input): the accidentally corrupted JPEG (valid JPEG header + trailing garbage) was accepted, stored as image/jpeg 1280x720, and its understanding described it as 'completely black with no visible subjects' — yet the browser cannot decode it at all ( onerror from the product's own media URL, while the other two images load fine). A merchant uploading a partially-corrupted photo would be charged for understanding, get a confidently wrong caption, and see a broken image. Not a money-path defect; noted because the caption is written into brand context (see finding above).
